mainTopic: Borrowed ingredients and ביטול, coal versus flame, and the תחום of water drawn from cisterns
overview: The amud opens with רב אשי's reason why borrowed spices, water and salt are not cancelled out in someone else's food: they are a דבר שיש לו מתירין. Two ברייתות about רבי יהודה seem to contradict the משנה. Each one is solved by splitting the cases: coarse salt versus fine salt, and a thick dish versus a thin, saucy one. Next, a new משנה and ברייתא teach that a coal is a real object and a flame is not, and they show how this matters for תחומין, הקדש, עבודה זרה, carrying on שבת, and vows. The גמרא explains that a הקדש flame is forbidden only by a rabbinic גזירה, because people do not naturally keep away from הקדש. רב ששת and אביי explain when carrying a flame does make one חייב: when it sits on a chip or shard too small to count by itself. Then the גמרא finds the case where one is פטור: a flame fanned outside by hand. A third משנה ties water drawn from a בור to the walking limits of the בור's owners. רב נחמן and רב ששת then argue whether a public cistern is ownerless or owned by partners, and רבא begins a challenge to רב נחמן that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אשי: something that will become permitted is never cancelled out
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different reason why the borrowed ingredients are not cancelled out: they are a דבר שיש לו מתירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The reason is that this is something that will become permitted later. Anything that will become permitted later is not cancelled out, even if it is only one part in a thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב אשי's own reason why borrowed spices, water and salt keep their owner's תחום limits even after being mixed into another person's dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on carrying these items past their owner's limits only lasts for the יום טוב. Once יום טוב is over, they may be taken anywhere. Since you can simply wait and the problem goes away, the רבנן did not let them be cancelled out (בטל), no matter how small the amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that will become permitted later on its own
Cancelled out, swallowed up by the larger mixture
Even in a thousand (even one part in a thousand)

steps.whyThisMatters: דבר שיש לו מתירין is a major rule across the laws of mixtures: if waiting will solve the problem, we do not rely on ביטול.

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said:
Because it is
a thing that will become permitted,
and anything that will become permitted
is not cancelled out, even in a thousand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reason, in place of the one given earlier on the daf, for why the ingredients are not cancelled out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ingredients bound by תחומין are a דבר שיש לו מתירין, so they are never cancelled out, even one part in a thousand.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה cancel out only water, or salt too?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says רבי יהודה exempts only water, which suggests salt is not cancelled out. But a ברייתא says he holds both water and salt are cancelled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי יהודה exempts water. That sounds like water is cancelled out but salt is not. But a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says water and salt are both cancelled out, whether in a dough or in a pot!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's words in the משנה. It then points out that a ברייתא seems to say the opposite about salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names only water, so we would conclude that salt stays bound to its owner's limits. The ברייתא says salt is cancelled out too. That is a direct contradiction about salt.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts (here: frees it from the תחום limit)
Water yes, salt no? (a conclusion drawn from what the משנה leaves out)
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Dough
Cooking pot, a cooked dish

phrases.english: "Rabbi Yehuda exempts in the case of water."
Water, yes; salt, no?
But isn't it taught:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Water and salt are cancelled out
whether in a dough or in a pot!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַיִם אִין, מֶלַח לָא? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the views of רבי יהודה in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion from the משנה that רבי יהודה holds salt is not cancelled out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying salt is cancelled out, so it contradicts what we inferred from the משנה.

steps.title: Coarse salt versus fine salt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about coarse salt from Sodom, which stays noticeable. The ברייתא is talking about fine salt, which dissolves.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one, the משנה, is about Sodom salt. That one, the ברייתא, is about fine isterokanit salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying each source is talking about a different kind of salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coarse salt can still be seen in the finished food, so it is not cancelled out. That is why the משנה did not include salt. Fine salt melts in and cannot be seen, so the ברייתא says it is cancelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (each source is about a different case)
This one ... that one
Coarse salt from Sodom
Fine salt that blends in

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about Sodom salt,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the משנה. The salt is coarse, so it stays noticeable.

phrases.english: that one is about isterokanit salt.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the ברייתא. The salt is fine, so it blends in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split the cases (each source is about a different kind of salt)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the two sources were about the same salt and disagreed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Coarse salt is not cancelled out. Fine salt is.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether something is cancelled out depends on whether you can still notice it in the finished food.

steps.title: A ברייתא says water is not cancelled out in a pot
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying water and salt are not cancelled out in a pot, because of its sauce. This contradicts the משנה, which says water is cancelled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: רבי יהודה says water and salt are cancelled out in a dough, but not in a pot, because of its sauce!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that seems to contradict the משנה, this time about water in a cooked dish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the משנה, רבי יהודה holds that water is cancelled out. Here רבי יהודה says that in a pot it is not cancelled out, because the liquid is still there in the sauce. So the two sources clash about water in a cooked dish.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught?
Sauce, the liquid of a cooked dish

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Water and salt are cancelled out in a dough,
but are not cancelled out in a pot
because of its sauce!
phrases.notes: The sauce is liquid, so the borrowed water can still be recognized.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second contradiction to the משנה. This one is about water in a pot, not about salt.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that רבי יהודה holds water is cancelled out, including in a cooked dish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying water is not cancelled out in a pot, because the sauce keeps it noticeable.

steps.title: Thick dish versus thin dish
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a thick dish with no sauce. The ברייתא is talking about a thin dish with sauce.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one, the משנה, is about a thick dish. That one, the ברייתא, is about a thin dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the second contradiction by again splitting the cases, this time by how thick the dish is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a thick dish the water soaks in and disappears, so it is cancelled out. In a thin dish the water stays as visible sauce, so it is not cancelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Thick (a dish without liquid)
Thin (a dish with liquid sauce)

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers follow one idea: an ingredient is cancelled out only when it disappears into the food.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this one is about a thick dish,
that one is about a thin dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּעָבָה, הָא בְּרַכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split the cases (thick dish versus thin dish)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought both sources were about the same kind of dish.
steps.terutzMaskana: Water is cancelled out in a thick dish but not in a thin, saucy one.

steps.title: משנה: a coal follows its owner, a flame goes anywhere
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a borrowed coal is limited to its owner's תחום, but a borrowed flame may be taken anywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A coal is like the feet of its owner, but a flame may go anywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a coal has real substance and a flame does not, starting with the laws of תחומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A coal is a real object, so it belongs to its owner and is limited to wherever he may walk. A flame lit from someone else's flame has no substance and takes nothing physical away from him. So it carries no limits.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A burning coal
A flame
Like the feet of the owner (limited to where he may walk)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A coal is like the feet of the owner,
phrases.notes: This means a coal borrowed on יום טוב may only go where its owner may walk.

phrases.english: and a flame may go anywhere.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It stays with the topic of borrowed items on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coal is limited to its owner's תחום. A flame is not.

steps.title: Coal and flame of הקדש
steps.stepSummary: Using a coal of הקדש makes a person liable for מעילה. A flame of הקדש should not be used, but using it is not מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a coal of הקדש, one is liable for מעילה. With a flame, one may not benefit from it, but one is not liable for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the same difference between coal and flame to rule on misusing holy property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה only applies to something with substance, so a coal counts and a flame does not. Still, the רבנן forbid benefiting from a holy flame in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: Property set aside for the בית המקדש
One is liable for מעילה (misusing holy property)
Benefit from (using it)

steps.confusionAlert: "לא נהנין ולא מועלין" does not mean a holy flame is fine to use. Using it is forbidden from the start; you just don't owe the מעילה penalty if you did.

phrases.english: A coal of consecrated property: one is liable for misusing it,
and a flame: one may not benefit from it, but one is not liable for misusing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second use of the coal-versus-flame difference, this time for הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coal of הקדש brings מעילה. A flame is forbidden to use but brings no מעילה.

steps.title: Carrying a coal or a flame on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Carrying a coal into רשות הרבים on שבת makes one liable. Carrying a flame does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who takes a coal out to the public domain is liable, but for a flame he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third result of the same difference, this time for the מלאכה of carrying on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying needs a real object that is moved from one domain to another. A coal is an object, so one is liable. A flame is not an object, so one is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes out (carries from one domain to another)
The public domain
Liable / exempt

steps.whatToRemember: All three rules in this משנה come from one idea: a coal has substance and a flame does not.

phrases.english: One who takes out a coal to the public domain is liable,
and for a flame, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third use of the coal-versus-flame difference, this time for carrying on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying a coal on שבת makes one liable. Carrying a flame does not.

steps.title: Five differences between a coal and a flame
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא listing five הלכות where a coal is treated as a real object and a flame is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: five things were said about a coal. A coal follows its owner's תחום, but a flame can go anywhere. Using a coal of הקדש is מעילה; a flame of הקדש may not be used, but using it is not מעילה. A coal of עבודה זרה is forbidden; a flame of it is permitted. Carrying a coal into רשות הרבים makes one חייב; carrying a flame is פטור. Someone forbidden by a נדר to benefit from his friend may not use his friend's coal, but may use his flame.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists five cases where a coal and a flame get different הלכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern in all five cases is the same: a coal is a solid thing that belongs to someone, so the full הלכה applies. A flame has no real body, so the הלכה is weaker or does not apply at all. The new items here are עבודה זרה and the person under a נדר.

keyTerms.meaning: A glowing coal, which is a real physical object
A flame, which has no solid body
Like the feet of the owner, meaning it may only go where the owner may go on יום טוב
One is liable for מעילה, misusing הקדש property
Idol worship, whose objects are forbidden to benefit from
Someone forbidden by a נדר to benefit from another person

steps.whatToRemember: In all five cases a coal is treated as a real thing and a flame is treated as almost nothing.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
Five things were said about a coal:
A coal is like the feet of the owner,
phrases.notes: On יום טוב it may only be carried within the owner's תחום, the area he himself may walk in.

phrases.english: but a flame may go anywhere.
A coal of הקדש: one is liable for misuse with it,
but a flame: one may not benefit from it, yet one is not liable for misuse.
A coal of idol worship is forbidden,
but a flame is permitted.
One who carries a coal out to the public domain is liable,
but for a flame he is exempt.
One who is forbidden by a vow to benefit from his friend
is forbidden to use his coal, but permitted to use his flame.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בַּגַּחֶלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the coal and flame rule of the משנה and adds more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coal carries full הלכה status in five areas; a flame has a weaker status or none.

steps.title: Why is a flame of עבודה זרה permitted but a flame of הקדש forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the ברייתא treats the two flames differently and asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a flame of עבודה זרה, that it is permitted, and what is different about a flame of הקדש, that it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the ברייתא: if a flame is not a real object, why is a הקדש flame still forbidden while an עבודה זרה flame is fully permitted? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the flame is not a real object, so the prohibition from the תורה should not apply to either. Yet the ברייתא says 'לא נהנין' for הקדש but 'מותרת' for עבודה זרה. The גמרא wants to know the reason for this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? The גמרא is asking for the reason two cases are treated differently
It is permitted
It is forbidden

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא שַׁלְהֶבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּשַׁרְיָא,
phrases.english: What is different about a flame of idol worship, that it is permitted,
and what is different about one of הקדש, that it is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא שַׁלְהֶבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּשַׁרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about an inconsistency between two lines of the ברייתא in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a flame of הקדש is forbidden while a flame of עבודה זרה is permitted.

steps.title: People already avoid idol worship, so no extra decree was needed
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן made a גזירה on a הקדש flame because people are not naturally careful with הקדש. With עבודה זרה, people stay away on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: עבודה זרה is disgusting and people keep away from it, so the רבנן did not make a גזירה about it. הקדש is not disgusting and people do not keep away from it, so the רבנן made a גזירה about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: a הקדש flame is forbidden only because of a rabbinic גזירה, and that גזירה was needed only for הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on a הקדש flame is only a rabbinic גזירה. People do not naturally keep away from הקדש, so the רבנן added a ban to guard it. Jews are disgusted by עבודה זרה and keep away on their own, so no extra גזירה was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Disgusting, repulsive
People keep away from it
The רבנן made a protective decree

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common rule: the רבנן add a גזירה only where people are likely to slip, not where they already stay away.

phrases.english: Idol worship, which is disgusting
and people keep away from it,
the Rabbis did not decree about it.
הקדש, which is not disgusting
and people do not keep away from it,
the Rabbis decreed about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, דִּמְאִיסָה וּבְדִילִי אִינָשֵׁי מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הקדש flame is forbidden only by a rabbinic גזירה, because people are not naturally careful with הקדש. With עבודה זרה people stay away on their own, so no גזירה was needed.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says carrying a flame makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the ברייתא's rule that carrying a flame is פטור, then challenges it with a ברייתא that says one is חייב for any flame.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: one who carries a coal into רשות הרבים is חייב, but for a flame he is פטור. But another ברייתא teaches: one who carries out a flame of any size is חייב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the carrying rule again and then attacks it with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא treats a flame as nothing, so carrying it on שבת is not הוצאה. The other ברייתא says even the tiniest flame makes one חייב. Both cannot be right as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא? This opens a contradiction
Any amount, even the smallest
The public domain, where carrying on שבת is forbidden

phrases.english: One who carries a coal out to the public domain is liable,
but for a flame he is exempt.
But was it not taught in a ברייתא:
One who carries out a flame of any size is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנְיָא: הַמּוֹצִיא שַׁלְהֶבֶת כׇּל שֶׁהוּא — חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the fourth item of the ברייתא in step 9 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that carrying a flame into רשות הרבים is פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא says carrying even a tiny flame makes one חייב, which contradicts the first.

steps.title: רב ששת: the flame was on a wood chip
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the second ברייתא is about a flame carried on a small piece of wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: the case is where he carried it out on a wood chip.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the contradiction by explaining what case the second ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flame by itself has no body, so carrying it is פטור, as our ברייתא says. But when the flame is burning on a chip, it is attached to something physical, so carrying it counts. The two ברייתות are talking about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A small wood chip or splinter
For example, the case is where

phrases.english: רב ששת said:
For example, where he carried it out on a wood chip.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהוֹצִיאוֹ בְּקֵיסָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: a flame alone compared to a flame on a chip
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seem to argue about whether carrying a flame counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: A flame alone is פטור; a flame carried on a chip is חייב.

steps.title: Then the chip itself should make him liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if he carried a chip, he should be חייב because of the chip, so why mention the flame?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him be חייב because of the chip!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's answer: if there is a chip, the chip alone should make him חייב, and the flame would not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא makes the flame the reason he is חייב. If the case has a chip, the ברייתא should have spoken about the chip, not the flame. So רב ששת's case does not seem to fit the wording of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him get it from, meaning there is already a simpler reason
Because of

phrases.english: But let him be liable because of the chip!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's explanation that the flame was carried on a chip.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a chip was carried, the chip itself should make him חייב, so the flame would not be the reason as the ברייתא says.

steps.title: The chip is too small to count on its own
steps.stepSummary: The chip is smaller than the minimum amount for carrying wood, which a משנה sets at enough to cook a small egg. So only the flame makes him חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a chip that does not have the minimum amount. As we learned in a משנה: one who carries out wood is חייב for enough to cook an easy-to-cook egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the chip is too small to make him חייב by itself, and backs this up with a משנה about the minimum amount of wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be חייב for carrying wood, it must be enough to cook a small egg. This chip is less than that, so the chip alone is פטור. The flame on top of it is what makes the carrying count, which is why the ברייתא speaks of the flame.

keyTerms.meaning: The minimum amount needed to be חייב
As we learned in a משנה
An easy-to-cook egg, a chicken egg
Wood

steps.whatToRemember: A flame alone is פטור. A flame on a chip too small to count by itself is חייב, because the flame gives the carrying importance.
steps.confusionAlert: The person is not חייב because of the chip. The chip is too small. He is חייב because of the flame, which counts here because it sits on a physical object.

phrases.english: Where it does not have the minimum amount.
As we learned in a משנה:
One who carries out wood
is liable for enough to cook an easy egg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 and makes רב ששת's answer hold up.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the chip is below the minimum amount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The chip alone should make him חייב, so the flame would be pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The chip is too small to cook an egg, so only the flame makes him חייב.

steps.title: אביי: A Flame Burning on an Oiled Vessel
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a different answer from רב ששת. The source that says one is חייב for a flame is talking about a vessel smeared with oil and lit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is talking about a case where someone smeared oil on a vessel and lit a fire on it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a second answer to the contradiction from step 12. He explains the source that makes one חייב in a different way from רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said the flame was on a tiny wood chip. אביי says instead that the flame burns on oil smeared on a vessel. Either way, the flame is attached to something, so carrying it can make him חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, a leading אמורא
he smeared it
oil
fire

phrases.english: Abaye said:
such as where he smeared a vessel with oil
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected wording, so read it as 'smeared the vessel.'

phrases.english: and lit a fire on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the contradiction from step 12, instead of רב ששת's wood chip.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources about carrying a flame seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source that says חייב is talking about a flame burning on oil smeared on a vessel.

steps.title: Why Not Be Liable for the Vessel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need the flame at all, since he carried the vessel and should be חייב for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he should be חייב because of the vessel itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי. If he carried a whole vessel, he is חייב for the vessel, so why mention the flame?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question the גמרא asked about the chip in step 14. If the object holding the flame is big enough to count by itself, the flame adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: let him get it from (a different reason)
a vessel

phrases.english: But let him be liable because of the vessel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's case from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's case of a flame on an oiled vessel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vessel is an important object, so carrying it makes him חייב anyway. Then the flame would not be the reason he is חייב.

steps.title: It Is a Piece of Earthenware
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the fire was on a broken piece of earthenware, not a whole vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a piece of earthenware.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'vessel' is really just a broken clay shard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken shard is not a full vessel. So it does not automatically make him חייב the way a whole vessel would.

keyTerms.meaning: a piece of broken earthenware, a clay shard

phrases.english: With an earthenware shard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by making the case narrower.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He carried a whole vessel, so he is חייב for the vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was only a shard, not a whole vessel.

steps.title: Why Not Be Liable for the Shard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes again: he should still be חייב for carrying the shard.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he should be חייב because of the shard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks that even a shard is an object, so carrying it should make him חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the vessel into a shard did not fully solve the problem. A shard can also be something one is חייב for carrying, so the flame still seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: because of

phrases.english: But let him be liable because of the shard!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that it was a shard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carrying a shard can also make him חייב, so the flame is still not needed as the reason.

steps.title: The Shard Is Below the Minimum Size
steps.stepSummary: The shard is smaller than the minimum size for carrying earthenware. A משנה sets that size at enough to place between window frames, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a shard that does not have the minimum size. As we learned in a משנה: for earthenware, the size is enough to put between one window frame and the next. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the shard is too small to count by itself. It brings a משנה to prove what the minimum size is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of object has a minimum size (שיעור) before carrying it makes one חייב. This shard is smaller than that, so only the flame makes him חייב. This matches the answer to the wood chip in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: the minimum amount needed to be חייב
as we learned in a משנה
earthenware
window frames (wooden boards)
רבי יהודה, a תנא

phrases.english: With one that does not have the minimum size.
As we learned: earthenware —
enough to put between one window frame and the next,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 and finishes defending אביי's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the case narrower, with a source for the minimum size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He is חייב for carrying the shard.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shard is below the minimum size, so only the flame makes him חייב.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב ששת and אביי say the same basic idea. A flame makes one חייב when it sits on something too small to count by itself.

steps.title: Then When Is Carrying a Flame Exempt?
steps.stepSummary: If a flame on almost anything makes one חייב, the גמרא asks when the rule that carrying a flame is פטור could ever apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about what we learned: 'One who carries out a flame is פטור'? How can that case ever happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the first rule, that carrying a flame is פטור. It asks what case that rule could still be talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flame usually burns on something, like a wick, a chip, or oil. If every such case makes him חייב, the rule of פטור seems to have nothing left to cover. So the גמרא asks for a real case that fits it.

keyTerms.meaning: a flame
exempt, not liable
how can you find this case?

phrases.english: But that which we learned:
One who carries out a flame is exempt,
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דִּתְנַן: הַמּוֹצִיא שַׁלְהֶבֶת פָּטוּר, הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answers of רב ששת and אביי to ask how the משנה's rule that carrying a flame is פטור (step 8) can ever apply.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that carrying a flame is פטור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a flame on any small object makes him חייב, there seems to be no case left where carrying a flame is פטור.

steps.title: He Fanned the Fire Outside with His Hand
steps.stepSummary: The פטור case is when he waved or fanned the flame by hand into the public area, without it being attached to anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where he fanned it with his hand into the public area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פטור rule is about a flame he pushed outside by waving his hand, with nothing holding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the flame moves into the public area by itself, without being attached to any object. A bare flame is not something real to carry, so he is פטור. This finishes the discussion of carrying a flame.

keyTerms.meaning: he fanned it (waved it along with his hand)
the public domain

steps.whatToRemember: A flame attached to a small object (a chip or an oiled shard) makes one חייב. A bare flame fanned outside by hand makes one פטור.

phrases.english: Such as where he fanned it with his hand into the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 and closes the topic of the flame.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no case left where carrying a flame is פטור.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is פטור when the flame is fanned out by hand, attached to nothing.

steps.title: New משנה: Water from a Cistern Follows Its Owners
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches how far water drawn from a בור may be carried on יום טוב. It depends on who owns the בור.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A private person's בור is like the feet of that person. A בור of the people of a town is like the feet of the people of that town. A בור of those who came up from Babylonia is like the feet of whoever fills from it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that water may only be carried as far as its owners may walk, and it gives three kinds of בור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Objects on יום טוב follow the walking limits (תחום) of their owners. Water from a private בור follows its owner. Water from a town בור follows the townspeople. Water from a public בור belongs to everyone, so it follows whoever draws it.

keyTerms.meaning: short for מתניתין, our משנה
a cistern or water pit
like the feet of, meaning it follows that person's walking limits
those who came up to ארץ ישראל from Babylonia
the one who fills (draws the water)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Like the feet of' does not mean the water itself walks. It means the water may be carried only where its owner is allowed to walk on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This continues the perek's main idea: on יום טוב, things are tied to the walking limits of the people they belong to.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A cistern of an individual is like the feet of the individual,
and one belonging to the people of that town
is like the feet of the people of that town,
and one of those who came up from Babylonia is like the feet of the one who fills.
phrases.notes: A public בור made for all travelers, so no one person owns it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בּוֹר שֶׁל יָחִיד כְּרַגְלֵי הַיָּחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the flame discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water drawn from a בור may be carried only within the walking limits of the בור's owner. Water from a public בור follows whoever draws it.

steps.title: Private cistern versus flowing rivers and springs
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the משנה ties a private בור to its owner's walking limits, while a ברייתא says flowing rivers and springs go with whoever draws the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised a contradiction to רב נחמן. Our משנה says water from an individual's cistern is like the feet of the individual. But another source says flowing rivers and gushing springs are like the feet of every person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. רבא sets two sources against each other: our משנה about a private בור, and a ברייתא about rivers and springs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, water from a private בור belongs to its owner, so it can only go as far as he may walk on יום טוב. But the ברייתא says water from rivers and springs follows whoever takes it. If a בור is also a water source, why doesn't its water follow the person who draws it?

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a contradiction, setting two sources against each other
Literally 'like the feet of'. The item may only go where that person may walk on יום טוב
An individual, a private owner
'And contrast it with', the phrase that brings in the opposing source
Flowing rivers
Springs that gush up from the ground

phrases.english: Gemara
Rava raised a contradiction to Rav Nachman:
We learned: a cistern of an individual
is like the feet of the individual,
phrases.notes: This means the water can only be carried as far as the owner himself may walk on יום טוב.

phrases.english: and contrast it with: flowing rivers
and gushing springs
are like the feet of every person!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה quoted in step 23 by challenging its first ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a private בור is like the feet of its owner
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water sources such as rivers and springs are treated as belonging to whoever draws from them. So why should a בור be different?

steps.title: The משנה is talking about collected water
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's private בור holds collected, standing water, not flowing water.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: What are we dealing with here? With collected water.
steps.whatsHappening: The contradiction is answered. The two sources are talking about different kinds of water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing water collected in a בור belongs to the owner, so it follows his feet. Flowing water passes through and is not anyone's property, so it follows whoever draws it. The two sources do not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What are we dealing with here?' The phrase introduces a narrower reading of a source
Collected, standing water, such as rainwater gathered in a pit

phrases.english: He said:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the name in round brackets.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With collected water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the משנה is about standing water, and the ברייתא is about flowing water
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be about the same kind of water source.
steps.terutzMaskana: A private בור of collected water follows its owner. Flowing water follows whoever draws it.

steps.title: שמואל says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A statement of שמואל, passed on by רבי חייא בר אבין, confirms that the משנה is about collected water.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of שמואל: with collected water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the answer by quoting an אמורא who gave the same explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new idea. It shows that the answer is not just a quick fix, because שמואל explained the משנה the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also stated', introducing an אמורא's statement that supports what was just said

phrases.english: And it was also stated:
Rabbi Chiya bar Avin said
that Shmuel said: with collected water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that the משנה is about collected water
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל, as reported by רבי חייא בר אבין
steps.whatToRemember: A private בור of standing water follows its owner's feet. Flowing rivers and springs follow whoever draws the water.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the public cistern
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: water from the cistern of עולי בבל follows whoever draws it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the cistern of those who came up from Babylonia is like the feet of the one who fills.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next ruling in the משנה. It is setting up an argument between אמוראים that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולי בבל dug these cisterns for public use. Because the water is public, it follows the person who draws it, not one particular owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who came up from בבל to ארץ ישראל. Their cisterns were for public use
The one who fills, the person who draws the water

phrases.english: And that of those who came up from Babylonia
is like the feet of the one who fills.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the private בור to the public cistern in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water from a public cistern follows the feet of whoever draws it.

steps.title: Water drawn for someone else
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב ששת argue about water one person draws and hands to another. Does it follow the one who receives it or the one who drew it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If someone filled water and gave it to his friend, רב נחמן says it is like the feet of the one it was filled for. רב ששת says it is like the feet of the one who filled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument between אמוראים about a new case connected to the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the water follows the one who fills. But what if he filled it for someone else? רב נחמן says it follows the friend who received it. רב ששת says it stays with the one who drew it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was stated', introducing a statement or argument of אמוראים
He filled water and gave it to his friend

phrases.english: It was stated: if one filled and gave to his friend,
Rav Nachman said:
like the feet of the one for whom they were filled;
Rav Sheshet said: like the feet of the one who filled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's public-cistern rule to water drawn for another person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: the water follows the one it was filled for. רב ששת: it follows the one who filled it.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רב נחמן and רב ששת disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the argument. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question asking for information, not an attack. The גמרא wants to find the underlying idea that splits the two אמוראים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'About what do they disagree?' The question that asks for the root of an argument

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the argument in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that explains the argument between רב נחמן and רב ששת

steps.title: Ownerless cistern or jointly owned cistern
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת holds that a public cistern is הפקר. רב נחמן holds that it belongs to all the people together as partners.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that the cistern is ownerless. The other master holds that the cistern belongs to partners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the argument depends on who owns a public cistern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cistern is הפקר, you cannot take ownerless property on behalf of someone else, so the water belongs to the one who drew it. That is רב ששת's view. If it belongs to partners, one partner can draw for another, so the water belongs to the friend right away. That is רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A cistern, the Aramaic word for בור
Ownerless property (הפקר)
Partners, people who own something together
'One master holds', the phrase that sets out each side of an argument

steps.confusionAlert: The first 'מר' (ownerless) is רב ששת and the second 'מר' (partners) is רב נחמן. This is the reverse of the order in which they were quoted in step 28.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a question about יום טוב carrying limits actually depends on a property question: who owns a public resource.

phrases.english: One master holds:
it is an ownerless cistern;
and one master holds:
it is a cistern of partners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument depends on whether a public cistern is ownerless (רב ששת) or jointly owned by partners (רב נחמן).

steps.title: רבא begins a challenge from a חרם vow
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן with a משנה: if someone says 'I am חרם to you', the one he said it to may not benefit from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised a challenge to רב נחמן: If one says, 'I am hereby חרם to you', the one prohibited by the vow is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a challenge against רב נחמן's view that a public cistern belongs to partners. Right now the גמרא is only setting up the source. The point of the challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה quoted is from נדרים. Someone who forbids himself to another person makes that person forbidden to get any benefit from him. רבא is preparing to use this vow case against רב נחמן's partnership idea.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a challenge from an earlier source (a משנה or ברייתא) against him
A strong kind of vow of prohibition
The person who is forbidden by the vow

phrases.english: Rava raised a challenge to Rav Nachman:
'I am hereby חרם to you',
phrases.notes: This is quoted from a משנה in נדרים. He is forbidding himself and his things to the other person.

phrases.english: the one prohibited by the vow is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an attack on רב נחמן's view, explained in step 30, that a public cistern belongs to partners.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that a public cistern is owned by partners
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is only the setup. רבא quotes the חרם vow משנה, and the challenge it raises against the partnership view comes next.
